A1.justification: Both PDFs present Video-3D LLM and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. The material supports reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations in Tables 2–4, and detailed results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a video-versus-voxel representation experiment in Table 5.

M1.justification: The stated grounding objective changes from a single positive object in v1 Equation 8 to a sum over positive objects in v2 Equation 7. This is a limited loss-formulation revision; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or experiments were rerun. The architecture and sampling algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Scan2Cap, ScanQA, and SQA3D. The new representation experiment uses retained tasks; newly cited indoor-scene datasets are not evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 Table 5 introduces a voxel-aggregation comparator using the same LLaVA-Video backbone as the proposed video representation. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark and appendix tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new representation experiment introduces a backbone-controlled comparison, averaging patch features within voxels and sampling 3,096 voxel features as LLM input. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets, and appendix evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds an ablation testing video versus voxel representations while holding the backbone fixed, plus a sampling-overhead measurement. The existing frame-sampling, positional-encoding, grounding-loss, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports voxel/video Scan2Cap CIDEr@0.5 scores of 54.9/83.8 and ScanQA EM of 28.1/30.1. V2 also reports 17.8 ms sampling overhead per ScanQA question. Table 1 swaps Grounded3D-LLM's Scan2Cap BLEU-4/CIDEr entries from 70.6/35.5 to 35.5/70.6. Existing proposed-method benchmark scores and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly defines positive-object and candidate-object sets and generalizes the grounding objective's numerator to multiple positives, which is mathematically different from v1's single-positive expression. Backprojection, positional encoding, and the greedy approximation argument otherwise remain equivalent; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim generalist 3D understanding through position-aware video representations, efficient maximum-coverage sampling, and state-of-the-art performance on the same five benchmarks. The rewritten introduction and conclusion retain these contribution claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new representation comparison as evidence for exploiting spatiotemporal priors rather than merely stronger visual features. It also shifts the positional-encoding discussion from strong performance without encoding toward encoding's consistent grounding and captioning benefits. Appendix B's limitation concerning similar objects in multi-target grounding is retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents construction of the voxel comparator, clarifies that LEO supplies Mask3D proposals for both grounding and captioning, and quantifies sampling overhead. Existing hardware, optimizer settings, code-access information, and appendix implementation details remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 removes the general 3D Scene Understanding related-work subsection and associated references, including ReferIt3D and Vote2Cap-DETR, while adding RIO and ScanNet++ citations as acquisition context. The central positioning against existing 3D LLMs and video-language approaches remains.

P1.justification: V2 revises portions of the introduction, method explanations, ablation discussion, and conclusion; renames Section 3.3 to Multi-Task Training; removes one related-work subsection; and adds acknowledgements. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains embedding labels, Table 3 reorders benchmark columns, and the new representation ablation appears as Table 5. Existing figures and tables are resized or reflowed locally, and appendix tables are renumbered without substantive display changes.

improvement.justification: The added backbone-controlled ablation strengthens evidence for the representation choice, while the revised grounding formula and proposal-source clarification improve transparency. Swapping the apparently transposed Table 1 baseline values improves internal consistency. The new discussion mistakenly describes the Scan2Cap improvement as going from 83.8 to 54.9, although Table 5 shows the reverse. This wording error limits polish but does not outweigh the modest gains.
